patch_description: The tightest bottleneck in Heilbronn-11 configurations is typically a small cluster of 3-4 points whose triangles bind simultaneously. Single-point moves cannot escape these "pair-traps" because moving either point alone decreases the min area even though moving both together increases it. I replace the random-jitter final polish in `_refine` with a structured greedy polish that (a) identifies the top-2 bottleneck triangles, (b) tries moving their involved points individually AND simultaneously along 12 fixed directions (plus opposites), and (c) continues scanning remaining directions at the same step size after an improvement before shrinking. This gives the optimizer a mechanism to escape coordinated constraints, which should raise the achievable min area. Since only bottleneck-involved points are moved (not all 11 × 12 directions), per-iteration cost stays modest, and the random 200-sample loop (which wastes evaluations on irrelevant points) is removed, recovering runtime.
